items.context: Dating and social startup; in five months, sole engineer across the Flutter app, NestJS backend (180+ APIs, 1,066 automated tests), and Docker deployment, maintaining two product lines (Sugarbee and Bound)
jobDesc: Built match suggestions, chat coaching, and icebreaker generation on the Anthropic API: JSON-constrained structured output with de-identified inputs, regex filtering on outputs, and three-tier merge-based degradation (AI output, profile templates, generic copy); timeouts calibrated to production P95 (4.5s → 8s after Sonnet shipped).

Wrote the team's AI development standard: where LLM calls belong architecturally, cost guardrails and policy red lines, versioned prompt directories with prompt changes treated as reviewable changes, and a rule that AI never blocks critical paths — payments, messaging, matching.

Put cost and concurrency guards around LLM calls: memory + Redis two-tier cache with version-prefixed keys for batch invalidation on prompt changes, and a distributed lock (TTL longer than the model timeout) before generation so duplicate requests don't each hit — and each pay for — the model.

Built the RAG support agent in Python (FastAPI) without LangChain: hybrid retrieval with RRF fusion, LLM reranking, two-tier caching, circuit breakers with provider failover; evaluation uses a golden dataset and LLM-as-a-Judge with Recall, MRR, and Groundedness running in CI.
Replaced runtime JSON parsing in the recommendation query with MySQL virtual generated columns and composite indexes: 5s → milliseconds, core APIs averaging 180ms.

Traced a connection-count alert to RDS Proxy losing multiplexing — frozen Lambda containers left sessions unterminated and connections pinned; shortening idle reclaim and adding connection validation and retries cut peak connections from 1,162 to 883 (−24%).

Moved static assets to S3 + CDN so Lambda no longer proxies static traffic, and with hero-image replacement and Chinese webfont subsetting took FCP from 10s to 1.4s; together with database right-sizing and caching, monthly cloud spend fell from US$1,200 to US$400 (−60%).
Split content moderation by media type — images synchronous, video through an async job queue — with real-person face verification.

Implemented subscription auto-renewal and failed-payment retries, and cross-referenced multiple signals to separate real cancellations from card-change interruptions; monthly revenue moved from NT$210K to NT$380K over that period.

items.context: Game and live-streaming platform; joined in 2020 as a backend engineer, promoted in late 2022 to lead 11 engineers across architecture and technical decisions for 12 product lines
jobDesc: Split each game format into API, Socket, business service, and async consumer, carrying peak-hour draw traffic of a thousand bets/orders per second and scaling at whichever tier is the bottleneck; Kafka for cross-service event streams, Redis and Bull Queue for caching and async settlement, Socket.IO for live rounds and draw results.
Took a proof-of-concept mini-game to production, then reused its shared services and delivery process across later titles, leading the team to 12 shipped product lines.
Added monitoring and logging (Sentry, Kibana, Grafana) and turned recurring troubleshooting into docs and saved queries, cutting problem isolation time by about 50%.
Turned release steps into a checklist and documented process so releases no longer depended on individual memory, reducing release defects by 70%.
Introduced design review before work starts and code review before merge so design and implementation defects are caught pre-release; both became the shared standard across product lines.

items.context: Same company, pre-promotion role; backend development and system analysis on a game and lottery platform, including taking over an unmaintained legacy system
jobDesc: Lead backend on the blockchain fair-random-number platform: combined multiple data sources into verifiable random numbers and wrote EOS smart contracts for on-chain proof, letting players verify draw results themselves.
Refactored an unmaintained inherited system into layered modules with shared logic extracted, so new game types extend the existing architecture without touching the core settlement flow.
Used slow-query logs to locate reporting and settlement bottlenecks, then added indexes and reworked queries and pagination, eliminating query timeouts during batch settlement.
Sole owner of lottery game types, the crawler data pipeline, and the operations dashboard — schema design through production operations.

items.context: Software consultancy; delivered 7 client engagements spanning requirements analysis through production operations
jobDesc: Moved transcoding and image blurring to AWS Lambda + FFmpeg as async jobs so long-running work no longer occupied application servers, and replaced manual releases with automated deployment.
Split frontend/backend responsibilities and redesigned APIs to cut coupling so both sides could work in parallel, with unit and functional tests covering regression after changes.
Delivered lending, video streaming, equipment repair, and e-commerce systems from zero to one — requirements analysis, system design, through production operations.
Chose stacks by the client's existing environment and timeline (C#, Node.js, React, Salesforce), extending current systems instead of rebuilding them.
First point of contact for new hires, maintaining environment setup and project docs to shorten onboarding.
